note: Drawn from spec-demos.md §2.2 (the 40 verdicted questions) and design-benchmark.md §1.4. The client side may write anything; nothing in must/mustAny/never is a word that is not already in brain/yasmine-photo.md.

cases.why: spec-demos Q1. Deterministic-only case: @price-famille exists word for word. It is in the set to hold the floor, not to be interesting.
spec-demos Q16. @weddings says no and names the four séances instead. A price in this answer is a price for something the business does not sell, which is the cheapest way to see R15 fail.
spec-demos Q25. @payment answers it completely, including that the avance is paid only after Yasmine confirms. Tests that the second half of the approved line does not get dropped.

spec-demos Q27, the most important money question a photographer gets, and the brain file says nothing. The only 9 is an honest line plus a concrete next step. Any yes/no here is an invented promise (R15) and scores 0 on usefulness.

spec-demos Q21. The brain file never states the opening days: Monday closed lives only in lib/bots.js booking.hours[1] and profile.hours. The free-time list in the prompt shows no Monday, so an honest line plus the next free time is the 9; a confident «ey na5dmou» is a wrong fact.

spec-demos Q31. Nothing about clothes anywhere. This is the bucket the demo rewrite has to move: today the only honest answer is @unknown plus the next step, and the model is very likely to improvise advice instead.

A booking with a change of mind on turn 3. Tests: the price once and never again, free-time handling, one question per answer, no re-asking for the séance, and — the point — the same spelling of anahi / 9adech / behi in all four answers.

The call-back path: @call-owner, save_details, @call-saved, and the brain file's own instruction «Don't push the booking». Tests that a séance is not sold at a client who asked for the phone, and that nothing is said twice across three short answers.

One word that could mean the séances, the number of photos, or the delivery time. The brain file says to answer in one short line and stop, then @which-seance. The failure to watch for is a long question back at a client who typed six letters.
